changelog: - **Relation and person children stay inside their tenant** (#2542). InteractionLog, RelationNote, MentorQuestion, MeetingRequest, Goal, Evaluation, StatusChange and ProjectTask carry no `orgId`, so the tenant middleware never scoped them, and with `MT_ENFORCE_ISOLATION` off (production) nothing did: an ADMIN of one org could list, read, edit, answer, decline, complete and delete another org's rows by id. `GET /api/interactions` now pins the caller's org onto the relation join via `orgScoped()`; every by-id handler (`/api/interactions/[id]`, `/api/relation-notes/[id]`, `/api/questions/[id]`, `/api/meeting-requests/[id]`, `/api/goals/[id]`, `/api/evaluations/[id]` PATCH and DELETE, `/api/status-changes/[id]`, `/api/project-tasks/[taskId]`) loads the parent's org and answers another tenant's row with the 404 a missing id gets, before any write (`goals/[id]` and `project-tasks/[taskId]` answered a missing id with 403 and now answer 404, so the two cases cannot be told apart); the relationId-taking routes (`/api/interactions` POST, `/api/interactions/summary`, `/api/relation-notes`, `/api/questions`, `/api/meeting-requests`, `/api/goals`, `/api/evaluations`, `/api/status-changes` POST) answer another tenant's relation like a missing one; and `/api/todos?userId=` no longer lets an admin reach a person of another org. The `evaluations/[id]` PATCH check was the flag-gated `assertSameOrg`, a no-op in production. The routes that query a registered model are now also wrapped in `withTenantScope`. Org-less callers and same-org callers see no change. Regression: `e2e/cross-tenant-relation-children.spec.ts`.
